body.statement: Whenever \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), the support-enumerated set \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}(Y_0,Y_1)\) is a measurable compact subset of \([-B,B]^N\), is computable by finitely many support-specific compact semialgebraic feasibility problems, is independent of \(\gamma\), and satisfies \(\inf_{\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)}\Pr_\vartheta\{\beta\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}(Y_0,Y_1)\}\ge0.95\). Empty and singleton outputs have Euclidean diameter zero. This guarantee includes positive-margin Gaussian instances with more affected units than the majority-valid-controls count in HeLiShiMiao2026 permits.
body.justification: A single set delivers finite-sample simultaneous coverage without a beta-min condition, support recovery, or known loading geometry.
body.gap: HeLiShiMiao2026 gives selection-based asymptotic coordinate inference under a majority-valid-controls count; this theorem gives finite-sample joint coverage on the stated Gaussian subclass throughout the unidentified union.
body.consumer: The construction yields joint and coordinate-projected uncertainty for the full RRSC interference map rather than isolated post-selection intervals.
body.proof_tex:
First consider the finite computation and regularity of the output.  For each one of the finitely many sets \(S\subseteq[N]\) with \(|S|\le s\), impose \(b_j=0\) for \(j\notin S\) and introduce variables \((b,P',m')\) satisfying
\[
-B\le b_j\le B,\; P'^{\top}=P',\quad P'^2=P',\quad
\operatorname{tr}(P')=r,\; P'm'=m',\quad
\lVert m'\rVert_2^2\le A^2,
\]
\[
\lVert P'-\widehat P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_0,\;
\lVert z-m'-b\rVert_2^2\le\varepsilon_1^2.
\]
The operator-norm inequality is semialgebraic, for example by requiring positive semidefiniteness of \(\delta_0^2I_N-(P'-\widehat P)^2\), expressed through its finitely many principal minors.  Hence this is exactly a finite list of compact semialgebraic feasibility problems, one per support, and its projection onto \(b\) is the defined set \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}\).  The variable domain is compact and all constraints are closed, so each projected set, and therefore their finite union, is compact.

For completeness, measurability does not require an unproved selection step.  The fixed tie rule makes \(Y_0\mapsto\widehat P\) Borel measurable, and \((Y_0,Y_1)\mapsto(\widehat P,z)\) is therefore Borel.  For a fixed support and a fixed closed subset \(K\) of the coefficient cube, minimize over the fixed compact domain consisting of \(b\in K\) on that support, rank-\(r\) projectors \(P'\), and \(m'\) in the radius-\(A\) ball the maximum of the continuous constraint violations
\[
\lVert P'-\widehat P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}-\delta_0,\;
\lVert P'm'-m'\rVert_2,\;
\lVert z-m'-b\rVert_2-\varepsilon_1.
\]
Its minimum is a continuous function of \((\widehat P,z)\), by uniform continuity on the fixed compact domain.  Feasibility is the event that this minimum is at most zero.  For an open set \(O\) in the coefficient cube, write \(O\) as the increasing union of the closed sets whose distance from \(O^c\) is at least \(1/n\).  The event that the output hits \(O\) is then a countable union, over \(n\) and the finitely many supports, of the preceding Borel feasibility events.  This proves compact-valued measurability.  The construction nowhere uses \(\gamma\).

Now fix \(\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\).  By the projector-region lemma,
\[
\Pr_\vartheta\{P\in\mathcal K_0(Y_0)\}\ge1-\alpha/2.
\]
By the post-mean law,
\[
{T_1\lVert\eta\rVert_2^2\over\sigma^2}\sim\chi_N^2.
\]
Since \(\sigma\le\sigma_{\mathrm{hi}}\), the definition of \(\varepsilon_1\) gives
\[
\Pr_\vartheta\{\lVert\eta\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_1\}\ge1-\alpha/2.
\]
On the intersection of these two events, take \(P'=P\), \(m'=m\), and \(b=\beta\).  The model assumptions give the support, cube, range, and radius constraints, while \(z-m-\beta=\eta\); hence \(\beta\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}\).  The union bound, without any independence requirement, proves coverage at least \(1-\alpha=0.95\), uniformly over the class.  By convention the diameter of an empty or singleton compact set is zero.

For the strict-regime example, take \(N=8,r=2,s=3\), let \(X\) have rows \((1,i)\), \(1\le i\le8\), and set \(U=X(X^{\top}X)^{-1/2}\).  Then \(U^{\top}U=I_2\).  Every two-row submatrix is nonsingular because
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}1&i\\1&j\end{pmatrix}=j-i\ne0\quad(i\ne j).
\]
There are finitely many such submatrices, so the equivalent deleted-row formula gives \(\kappa_3(\operatorname{col}(U))>0\).  Choosing any sufficiently small vector with exactly three nonzero coordinates supplies a legal positive-margin Gaussian instance covered by the theorem.  HeLiShiMiao2026, Assumption 4 and its identification discussion, impose the majority-valid-controls count whose \(N=8,r=2\) specialization permits at most two affected units; thus this three-effect instance establishes the final comparison.
